specGaps: SG-A — TEST VEHICLE AND GATE LEG (the one that decides whether 14.1's red is observable at all). Plan:86 mandates stdlib `unittest`, but STATE.json records 14.1's canonicalTestCmd as `bash scripts/test-conductor.sh`, which at HEAD runs node/tsc/bun/export-schemas and no Python. RESOLUTION: the unit suite lands at `scripts/test_conductor_bench.py` and is picked up by the python leg Task 12.1's PROMOTED spec adds to scripts/test-conductor.sh — `/usr/bin/python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'`, placed after the schema-export leg (docs/build/specs/task-12.1.assertions.json, row 12.1-python-test-leg and its 'test location and the gate leg' gap). 14.1 therefore adds NOTHING to test-conductor.sh when 12.1 has landed: the discovery pattern already matches. If 14.1 somehow runs first, the ORCHESTRATOR adds that exact leg (test-conductor.sh is orchestrator-owned; the implementer never edits it) — the same leg, not a second runner. REASONING: one gate command is the build's whole evidence discipline; a Python suite the gate cannot see is a suite that will silently rot, and two discovery roots is that failure with extra steps.

SG-B — WHERE THE 10 TASK REPOS AND THEIR HIDDEN TESTS LIVE. The plan's §1.1 tree (line 402) lists exactly one new file under bench/ — conductor-tasks.json — yet each task needs a seed repository and a hidden test that must never be visible to the model. RESOLUTION: both are carried INLINE in the manifest as `seedFiles` and `hiddenFiles` maps of repo-relative path → file content. §1.1 stays literally true (one new file under bench/), seeding and hidden-copy become pure string→files functions the unit suite can exercise with no fixture directories, and the hidden material lives in a file the model never sees because the model only ever sees a seeded scratch copy. ALTERNATIVE REJECTED: `bench/repos/<taskId>/` + `bench/hidden/<taskId>/` directory trees — two new directories the plan's tree does not list, and a second place for a path to drift out of sync with the manifest that names it. COST ACCEPTED: the manifest is a large JSON file; the tasks are one-function to small-multi-file by the plan's own selection criteria, so this is measured in tens of kilobytes.

SG-C — PER-CELL TOKEN ATTRIBUTION. The plan requires all arms to run 'through the router so token accounting is uniform' (plan:2991) but 11.7's PROMOTED ledger line carries neither a timestamp nor a run id, and the baseline/doctrine arms send no X-Conductor-* headers at all, so there is no field to group by. RESOLUTION: attribute by LEDGER WINDOW — before a cell starts, record the ledger's current line count N0; after the cell's process exits, read lines N0..end. This is exact only if cells never overlap, so the driver executes cells STRICTLY ONE AT A TIME (which the plan's design already implies: one local 27B, one server) and the run plan carries no concurrency knob. ALTERNATIVE REJECTED: filtering by X-Conductor-Group — works only for the conductor arm, which would make the arms' cost numbers non-comparable, defeating the purpose of routing all arms through the router. REASONING: a wrong token number is worse than a missing one, so an unreadable/absent ledger yields nulls plus `tokensPartial: true`, never a silent zero.

SG-D — WHAT 'THE DOCTRINE PACKS INJECTED AS A SYSTEM PROMPT' MEANS CONCRETELY (plan:2996). The doctrine arm has no roles, so inject.ts's role→pack mapping has nothing to select on, and there is no plugin to call buildSystemAppend. RESOLUTION: the bench concatenates ALL nine conductor/doctrine/*.md files, in sorted filename order, each preceded by a `# <filename>` separator line, into ONE generated file inside the cell directory, and references it with a SINGLE `{file:<abs path>}` in the arm config's agent prompt (wire-notes:31 verifies that a {file:} agent prompt becomes the system message). One reference rather than nine avoids relying on unverified multi-reference resolution. The pack list is read from the DIRECTORY, not hardcoded, so adding a tenth pack changes the doctrine arm automatically. REASONING: the arm's job is to measure the cheap intervention (better prompting) at full strength; withholding packs would understate it and make the conductor arm's margin look larger than it is.

SG-E — WHO STARTS llama-server AND llama-router. Plan:2991 assumes both are up; no 14.1 bullet starts either, and 12.1 is the task that gives serve.py `--router`. RESOLUTION: conductor_bench.py starts NEITHER. It takes the router base URL and the metrics ledger path as inputs (defaulting to the values in `.data/configs/conductor-router.json`, the file 12.1 generates), and PRECHECKS before the first cell: GET /conductor/health answers 200, the model id is listed by GET /v1/models through the router, and the ledger path exists and is readable. A failed precheck exits nonzero naming the remedy (`scripts/serve.py --router`) BEFORE spending an overnight. REASONING: a bench that starts its own server owns a lifecycle it cannot supervise (serve.py execs into the session shell for exactly this reason, §4.4), and a 90-run job that discovers a dead router at run 47 has burned the night.

SG-F — HEADLESS PERMISSION PROMPTS. conductor/opencode-fragment.json sets `edit: "ask"` on the orchestrator agent and `question: "ask"` on the sub-agents; `opencode run` is non-interactive, and wire-notes:32 records that the typed `permission.ask` plugin hook is NOT dispatched at 1.18.15, so nothing in-process answers a prompt. RESOLUTION: every arm is invoked with the IDENTICAL flag set including `--auto` (auto-approve permissions that are not explicitly denied — the fragment's `git commit *` / `git push *` denies survive it, so the gates that matter stay gates), and every cell carries a hard wall-clock timeout as the backstop. The invariant the tests enforce is flag IDENTITY across arms, not the specific value: if 14.2 discovers `--auto` is wrong, it changes in one place for all three arms. REASONING: an arm that hangs on a prompt and an arm that does not would be measuring the harness's ergonomics, not the process.

SG-G — METRICS THAT ONLY ONE ARM CAN PRODUCE. schema-retry counts, review findings, overrides used and terminal stop kind (plan:2998-2999) exist only where the plugin runs. RESOLUTION: those four fields are `null` for baseline and doctrine — structurally inapplicable — and an integer (possibly 0) for conductor. The report renders null as `n/a` and NEVER as 0. REASONING: printing 'conductor caught 12 findings, baseline caught 0' is a category error dressed as a result; baseline has no reviewer to catch anything, and the plan's 'never a bare aggregate delta' (plan:3001) is the same instinct applied to pass rates.

SG-H — WHAT 'SCORING PASS-THROUGH' IS (plan:2982, undefined in the plan). RESOLUTION: the score is the hidden test command's exit status passed through unchanged — exit 0 is a pass, any nonzero is a fail, a timeout or spawn failure is a fail recorded under a distinct `outcome` so it is never confused with a model failure. No model judge, no partial credit, no ratio. ALTERNATIVE REJECTED: reusing benchmark.py's score_exec ratio (passed/total parsed from an inline harness) — it is built for single-file generated Python, not a repo-level test command, and a ratio invites a 'mostly passing' story the POC has no business telling. REASONING: the plan's collected field is 'hidden-test pass/fail' (plan:2998) — binary, objective, and the one number a reader can check.

SG-I — 'FAILS ON AN UNMODIFIED REPO' CANNOT BE A UNIT-SUITE ASSERTION. Plan:2988 requires every hidden test to fail on the unmodified repo, but proving it means running 10 real test commands across three toolchains (node, /usr/bin/python3 -m pytest, cmake/ctest) inside the gate. RESOLUTION: the unit suite asserts what is cheap and total — the manifest parses, every hidden command's argv[0] resolves, every seed/hidden path is well-formed and disjoint — and a fully implemented `--verify-tasks` subcommand seeds each task and runs its hidden command against the UNMODIFIED seed, requiring a nonzero exit from every one and exiting nonzero if any hidden test passes unmodified. That mode is run once by Task 14.2 and its output recorded. This is NOT a G4 stub: the mode is implemented and executable, it is simply not a gate leg because it needs toolchains the gate does not guarantee.

SG-J — THE MODEL IDENTIFIER. G13 requires one model across arms; the plan names `qwen3.6-27b` (plan:2964, 3007) while opencode needs `provider/model`. RESOLUTION: the model is ONE parameter, defaulting to `llamacpp/qwen3.6-27b` (verified from .data/configs/opencode.json's provider key + model id), threaded into all three arm configs AND every `opencode run -m` invocation from that single value. A test that changes the parameter must change all three arms; no arm may carry a literal model string.

SG-K — RUN ORDER ACROSS 90 CELLS. The plan gives the multiplicands, not the order, and order matters for an overnight that may be interrupted. RESOLUTION: repetition-major, arm-interleaved within a task — for rep in 1..3, for task in manifest order, for arm in (baseline, doctrine, conductor). An abort therefore leaves the arms BALANCED (each arm equally represented for every completed task) rather than 30 baseline runs and nothing to compare them to, and drift in machine state (thermal, cache) is spread across arms instead of concentrated in one.

SG-L — SAMPLING DIFFERS BETWEEN ARMS BY CONSTRUCTION. The conductor arm gets inject.ts:48-56's per-role temperatures (0.1–0.7); baseline and doctrine have no roles. RESOLUTION: baseline and doctrine set NO temperature override (opencode's default for the model), because the doctrine arm's definition is 'the doctrine packs injected as a system prompt, no gates, no fan-out, no FSM' (plan:2996) — sampling policy is part of the pipeline, not part of the prompting. The report states this explicitly in its methodology section so a reader is not misled into thinking the arms were sampling-matched. REASONING: silently matching temperatures would change what the conductor arm IS; silently not disclosing it would be the confound the three-arm design exists to remove.

SG-M — A CONDUCTOR-ARM CELL WHERE THE PLUGIN NEVER LOADED. wire-notes:73-76 and honest-limit 11 (plan:3087-3091): a plugin whose factory throws is logged and the session continues UNGATED and normal-looking. Such a cell is a baseline run wearing the conductor arm's label. RESOLUTION: after a conductor-arm cell, the absence of any `.conductor/runs/*` directory sets `pluginAbsent: true`; those cells are counted and named in the report under their own heading and excluded from the conductor arm's pass rate. REASONING: scoring a silent ungate as a conductor result measures the wrong thing in the direction that flatters the build, which is the one direction a POC must not be wrong in.

assertions.text: `load_tasks(path)` reads bench/conductor-tasks.json and returns exactly 10 task records. The manifest is an object {version: 1, selectionCriteria: {...}, defaults: {model, runTimeoutSec}, tasks: [...]} and every task carries: id (unique, non-empty), language ('ts'|'python'|'cpp'), difficulty ('one-function'|'multi-file'), behavioral (bool), rationale (non-empty string stating why this task is in the set), prompt (non-empty — the ONLY text handed to the model), seedFiles (non-empty map of repo-relative path -> file content), hiddenFiles (non-empty map of repo-relative path -> file content), hiddenTestCommand (non-empty LIST of argv strings), repoTestCommand (list of argv strings — the visible runner the seeded repo ships), behavioralPaths (list of glob strings). Each of the following inputs raises BenchError whose message names both the offending task id and the offending field, and no other input does: a missing required key; language 'rust'; difficulty 'medium'; a duplicate id; hiddenTestCommand given as the string 'pytest tests' instead of a list; a seedFiles path that is absolute or contains '..'; a tasks array of length 9 or 11. A well-formed manifest parses with no exception and preserves task order.

the committed bench/conductor-tasks.json satisfies plan:2985-2988's stated criteria, asserted as properties of the loaded set rather than trusted prose: all three languages 'ts', 'python' and 'cpp' each appear at least once; at least two tasks have behavioral == false (the docs/comment path, so the non-behavioral trajectory is measured too); both difficulty values 'one-function' and 'multi-file' appear at least once; every task's rationale is non-empty; and the manifest's top-level selectionCriteria block is present and non-empty. The same test reads the criteria from the parsed manifest, so a future edit that drops the last C++ task or the second non-behavioral task fails this row rather than silently narrowing the benchmark.

every task's hiddenTestCommand and repoTestCommand is spawnable WITHOUT being run: argv[0] either resolves via shutil.which or is an absolute path to an existing executable file, and the check is performed by a pure predicate over the argv list (no subprocess is started by this test). A manifest entry whose argv[0] is 'definitely-not-a-real-runner' is reported as unspawnable, naming the task id and the command; every entry in the committed manifest passes. Commands are argv LISTS everywhere and are never joined into a shell string — no code path in conductor_bench.py passes shell=True.

the hidden tests are never shown to the model, enforced structurally: for every task, the key sets of seedFiles and hiddenFiles are DISJOINT; the pure function that computes a cell's seeded file set returns exactly seedFiles' paths and contains no hiddenFiles path; and the task's prompt string contains none of the hiddenFiles paths and none of their basenames. Additionally the driver's ordering is asserted through an injected fake runner that records call order: hidden files are materialized into the cell's work tree only AFTER the opencode process has exited, and never before it starts.

`conductor_bench.py --verify-tasks` is implemented (not a stub) and enforces plan:2988's 'FAILS on an unmodified repo': for each task it seeds a scratch copy from seedFiles alone, materializes hiddenFiles, runs hiddenTestCommand in that copy, and requires a NONZERO exit. It prints one line per task with the observed exit code, exits 0 only when every task's hidden test failed on the unmodified seed, and exits nonzero naming every task whose hidden test PASSED unmodified (such a task measures nothing). Driven in the unit suite against a two-entry synthetic manifest in a temp dir whose commands are trivial shell-free argv (one exiting 1, one exiting 0), asserting the exit code and the named task in both directions.

the arm vocabulary is the closed tuple ARMS == ('baseline', 'doctrine', 'conductor') in that order, exported as module data so every consumer iterates one list; build_arm_config raises BenchError naming the unknown value for any other arm string, and the run plan contains cells for exactly these three and no others.

G13 is structural, not a convention: build_arm_config takes the model identifier as ONE parameter and every arm's generated config resolves to that identifier (default 'llamacpp/qwen3.6-27b'); building all three arms with model='llamacpp/qwen3.6-27b' yields three configs whose model selection strings are byte-identical, and rebuilding with a different value changes all three. No arm-specific branch may supply a model literal — asserted by building with a sentinel model string and requiring that string to appear in all three configs and that no other model id appears in any of them.

the baseline arm is plain opencode: its generated config contains NO 'plugin' key at any depth, none of the seven conductor-* agent definitions from conductor/opencode-fragment.json, and its serialized form contains no substring drawn from any conductor/doctrine/*.md file (checked against the first non-empty line of each of the nine packs). It does carry the provider block and the model, so the only thing it lacks is conductor.

the doctrine arm injects the doctrine and nothing else: the bench writes ONE generated file into the cell directory that is the byte concatenation of every *.md file in conductor/doctrine/, in sorted filename order, each preceded by a '# <filename>' separator line, and the arm config's agent prompt is a single '{file:<absolute path to that generated file>}'. The generated file contains each pack's full text verbatim (asserted by reading the nine files from the tree and requiring each one's exact bytes to appear); the pack list comes from a directory listing, so adding a tenth .md file to a temp doctrine dir adds it to the generated prompt without a code change. The doctrine arm config contains NO 'plugin' key and none of the conductor-* agents.

the conductor arm's config is produced by Task 12.1's committed fragment merge over conductor/opencode-fragment.json — the bench imports that function rather than re-implementing a merge — so the measured arm cannot drift from what serve.py ships: the result carries the absolute plugin path (wire-notes:21's verified loading form) with no '${LLAMA_HARNESS_ROOT}' left anywhere in its serialized form, carries the seven conductor-* agent definitions, and does NOT inline doctrine pack text (the plugin injects doctrine at runtime via buildSystemAppend). Asserted by building the arm against a temp harness root and diffing the merged keys against the fragment file read from the tree.

for one task, the three arm configs are compared key-by-key and differ ONLY in the plugin/agent/prompt keys that define the arm: provider block, baseURL, model selection, and every other key are byte-identical across the three; and the cell inputs that are not config — the task prompt string, the seeded file set, the opencode CLI flag list (except the config path), and the environment variable names — are identical across arms. This is the experiment's control, so it is asserted as an equality over the built objects rather than left to review.

all three arm configs point their provider options.baseURL at the ROUTER's listen host:port (formatted 'http://<host>:<port>/v1', matching scripts/serve.py:217's shape), taken from the parsed router config passed in, never at llama-server's upstream port and never hardcoded — so token accounting is uniform across arms (plan:2991). Building the arms against a router config with listen port 9099 puts 9099 in all three configs and the upstream port in none of them.

no generated arm config can 400 opencode: every '{file:<path>}' reference appearing ANYWHERE in any built config's serialized form (opencode scans every config string — wire-notes:31) names an absolute path that exists on disk at the moment the config is written, and so does the conductor arm's plugin path. A doctrine build whose generated pack file is deleted before validation, and a conductor build whose plugin path does not exist, are each rejected by the bench with a BenchError naming the missing path — rather than being handed to opencode, where a dangling reference is a hard ConfigInvalidError that would silently kill every remaining cell of that arm. For the conductor arm this is 12.1's committed existence check (row 12.1-file-refs-exist) rather than a second implementation; the bench's own check covers the doctrine arm's generated file, which 12.1 knows nothing about.

every arm config pins opencode auto-update OFF ('autoupdate': false at the top level — the key 12.1's promoted spec pins for the same reason, row 12.1-autoupdate-off, per the C-012 ruling), so a 90-run overnight cannot have opencode update itself mid-benchmark and silently invalidate the 1.18.15 wire contract every arm was constructed against. Asserted on all three built configs; a run whose recorded opencode version differs from the version recorded at precheck is flagged in the report rather than averaged in.

the pure environment builder for a cell returns a mapping containing OPENCODE_CONFIG (the cell's arm config), XDG_CONFIG_HOME, OPENCODE_TEST_HOME and XDG_STATE_HOME, with the latter three all pointing INSIDE that cell's own directory (wire-notes:20's verified hermetic triple, plus state isolation so one cell's stale-red registry, quarantine and worktrees cannot reach another's). Two different cells produce four pairwise-different paths; the same builder is used for all three arms and differs between them only in the OPENCODE_CONFIG value; and the user's own HOME/XDG values are not propagated into any of those four variables.

build_run_plan(tasks, ARMS, reps=3) returns exactly 90 cells for the 10-task manifest: cell ids are unique and formatted '<arm>/<taskId>/r<n>' with n in 1..3, every (arm, task) pair appears exactly 3 times, and every task appears 9 times. Ordering is repetition-major and arm-interleaved (rep, then task in manifest order, then arm in ARMS order), so truncating the plan at ANY prefix length leaves the three arms' counts differing by at most the number of arms within the current task — asserted by taking prefixes of several lengths and comparing per-arm counts. The function takes reps as a parameter (3 by default) and produces 3 x len(tasks) x len(arms) cells for other values.

an overnight that dies is resumable: a cell whose result file already exists under the results directory is SKIPPED (its recorded result is reused verbatim, nothing is re-run and no work tree is re-seeded), and `--report-only` executes zero cells and rebuilds the report purely from the result files on disk. Driven with an injected fake runner that counts invocations: with 90 planned cells and 12 result files present, a resumed run invokes the runner exactly 78 times; --report-only invokes it 0 times and still emits a complete report over the 12.

each cell gets a FRESH work tree so repetitions are independent: seeding a cell removes any existing directory at that cell's path and re-materializes seedFiles from the manifest, then initializes a git repo with a single initial commit containing exactly the seeded files (conductor needs a startHead and a clean tree; plan §2.3's startHead/startBranch/startDirty). Two cells of the same task never share a directory, and seeding a cell twice — with a junk file written in between — yields a tree whose tracked content equals the seed and whose git status is clean, so repetition 2 can never inherit repetition 1's edits.

a conductor-arm cell never blocks on the first-run setup questions (plan:2903 — git mode and behavioralPaths confirmation are the two questions with NO default): before the run, the bench writes the cell's .conductor/config.json from a pure function of the manifest task — verify/itemTest command from the task's VISIBLE repoTestCommand (never the hidden one), behavioralPaths from the task, git mode set explicitly — and the same function produces the same config for all three repetitions of that task. Asserted by building the config for a behavioral and a non-behavioral task and checking that the hidden command's argv appears nowhere in the emitted config.

a hung cell cannot eat the overnight: each cell runs under a wall-clock timeout (manifest defaults.runTimeoutSec, per-task overridable) and on expiry the driver terminates the whole PROCESS GROUP (opencode spawns children), records outcome 'timeout' with passed false and a wallClockMs at least the timeout, and proceeds to the next cell. Driven against a real short-lived subprocess in a temp dir (a shell-free argv that sleeps well past a sub-second timeout): the call returns rather than hanging, the recorded outcome is 'timeout', and no descendant of the spawned process is still alive afterwards.

every cell's result is written to its own file the moment the cell finishes — '<results dir>/<arm>__<taskId>__r<n>.json', one writer per file — so a crash loses at most the cell in flight. The results directory defaults to .data/benchmark/conductor/runs/ and the report to exactly .data/benchmark/conductor-report.md (plan:3001), both overridable by parameter, and every write in the unit suite goes to a tempfile directory: no test writes anywhere under .data/. The driver writes only inside its results directory and that one report file, and never touches the pre-existing .data/benchmark/report.md or the per-model directories beside it.

a cell result validates against one pinned schema with EVERY key present and inapplicability expressed as null (never a missing key, never a stand-in zero): cellId, arm, taskId, rep, startedIso, outcome ('pass'|'fail'|'timeout'|'harness-error'), passed (bool), exitCode (int|null), wallClockMs (int), tokens {prompt:int|null, completion:int|null, total:int|null, partial:bool}, routerErrors (int), schemaRetries (int|null), reviewFindingsUpheld (int|null), overridesUsed (int|null), stopKind (string|null), pluginAbsent (bool|null). A result missing any key, or carrying a stopKind outside conductor/core/stops.ts's closed STOP_KINDS vocabulary (done|noop|blocked|surfaced|env|interrupt), is rejected by the validator naming the field; a well-formed result round-trips through write and read unchanged.

scoring is a pure pass-through of the hidden test command's exit status and nothing else: exit 0 -> {passed: true, outcome: 'pass'}; any nonzero exit -> {passed: false, outcome: 'fail', exitCode: <that code>}; a timeout -> {passed: false, outcome: 'timeout'}; a spawn failure -> {passed: false, outcome: 'harness-error'}. There is no ratio, no partial credit, no parsing of test output for counts, and no model-graded path anywhere in the module (a grep of conductor_bench.py finds no judge/self-score call). The scorer is a pure function of (exit code, timed-out flag, spawn-error flag) and never re-reads the work tree.

token totals come from the router ledger window for the cell, computed purely: given the ledger's line count before the cell and the ledger's lines after it, summarize_ledger_window returns prompt/completion/total as the sums of promptTokens/completionTokens over the window's lines (11.7's pinned camelCase keys), skipping nulls; if ANY line in the window carries a null promptTokens or completionTokens, or the ledger is absent or unreadable, partial is true (and totals are null when nothing at all could be read) — the count is never quietly under-reported. A window computed over a fixture ledger of hand-written lines yields exact hand-computed totals, and a window of zero lines yields totals 0 with partial true, because a cell that produced no ledger line means the router saw no request.

infrastructure failures are visible rather than averaged in (G5): summarize_ledger_window counts ledger lines whose `status` is not 2xx into routerErrors — 502 (upstream unreachable), 503 (admission shed/queue timeout) and any 5xx alike — and a cell with routerErrors > 0 is marked in its result and listed by cell id in the report's own section. Such a cell's pass/fail is still recorded, but the report names it, so a night where the server fell over cannot be read as a model result. Asserted over a fixture ledger mixing 200/502/503 lines with hand-computed counts.

the conductor arm's process metrics are read from the run directory the plugin wrote (plan §1.2:418-440), by exactly these derivations: schemaRetries = the number of journal.jsonl lines with component 'fanout' and event 'subsession.retry' (conductor/adapter/fanout.ts:304 — the only schema-retry record in the system); overridesUsed = run.json's counters.overridesUsed (conductor/core/types.ts:205); stopKind = run.json's stop.kind when stop is non-null, else the terminal run state (REPORTED|TRIVIAL_DONE|ANSWERED) when the run is terminal, else null; reviewFindingsUpheld = the count of upheld findings across runs/<runId>/reviews/*.json, 0 when the run directory exists but has no reviews/. All four are read from the single newest directory under .conductor/runs/, and the collector never imports TypeScript or re-derives a value the plugin already recorded (G6). Driven against a fixture .conductor tree with hand-written journal/run/review files.

for a baseline or doctrine cell, schemaRetries, reviewFindingsUpheld, overridesUsed and stopKind are null — structurally inapplicable, because no plugin ran — and the collector does not go looking for a .conductor directory for those arms. They are never 0: a test builds one result per arm from the same fixture and asserts null for the two non-conductor arms and an integer for conductor, and asserts that the report renders the null cells as 'n/a'.

a conductor-arm cell that produced NO .conductor/runs/* directory records pluginAbsent true (honest-limit 11 / wire-notes:73-76: a plugin whose factory throws leaves a session that looks completely normal and is entirely ungated). Such cells are excluded from the conductor arm's pass-rate numerator and denominator and are listed by cell id under their own report heading with a count; the report's conductor pass rate over a fixture set containing two pluginAbsent cells is computed over the remaining cells and states how many were excluded. For baseline and doctrine cells pluginAbsent is null.

aggregate(results) reports spread, not just means: for every (arm, task) cell group it yields passes (int), reps recorded (int), the per-repetition outcome vector in repetition order (e.g. ['pass','fail','pass']), and min/max pass over those repetitions; for every arm it yields the totals across tasks plus the per-task pass counts. Asserted against a hand-built 30-cell fixture with exact expected numbers, including one (arm, task) group that is 3/3, one that is 0/3 and one that is 1/3 — so a 1/3-vs-2/3 difference can never be presented as if it were a stable one.

render_report never emits a bare aggregate delta (plan:3001): the rendered markdown contains a per-task table with one row per task and a column per arm, each cell showing 'k/3' AND that group's per-repetition outcome vector, for EVERY task present in the results — and any arm-level total or arm-to-arm comparison line appears only in a section that also contains that table. Asserted by rendering the 30-cell fixture and checking that all 10 task ids appear as rows, that every rendered arm total is accompanied by the per-task rows, and that removing the per-task rows from the fixture (a results set with one arm only) does not produce a comparison sentence at all.

an incomplete set is reported as incomplete: rendering results for 62 of 90 planned cells states 'recorded k of n' per arm and per task, names the missing cell ids in their own section, and computes every rate over RECORDED cells only — missing cells are never counted as failures, never counted as passes, and never silently dropped from a denominator that still claims to be 3. Asserted by rendering a fixture whose plan is 30 cells but whose results are 22, with hand-computed per-task 'k/n recorded' strings.

the report carries the cost side and its own methodology, because the POC's deliverable is quality delta VERSUS cost (plan:3018-3021): per arm and per task it renders total and median wall-clock and total tokens (marked partial wherever any contributing cell had tokens.partial true), and it states in prose the model used, the arm definitions, the repetition count, that all arms ran through the router, and that baseline/doctrine cannot produce the four conductor-only metrics. Asserted by rendering the fixture and requiring the model identifier, the three arm names, the repetition count and the partial-token marker to be present with hand-computed totals.

the module obeys G1/G3/G4 mechanically: conductor_bench.py imports only the Python standard library plus repo-local sibling modules (asserted by parsing the module's own import statements with the ast module and checking every top-level module name against sys.stdlib_module_names plus the allowed local names), it imports and runs under /usr/bin/python3 3.9.6 (so `from __future__ import annotations`, typing.Optional/Dict/List, and no `match` statement or PEP 604 runtime unions), the entire unit suite runs with no subprocess started except the deliberately-scoped timeout and --verify-tasks rows and with no network access, and every pure function named in this spec (load_tasks, build_arm_config, build_run_plan, summarize_ledger_window, the scorer, aggregate, render_report) executes with no filesystem write. No arm, mode or metric is left unimplemented behind a placeholder: a grep of the committed module finds no TODO, FIXME, 'not implemented' or pass-only function body.
